newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt flat as market winds down before break.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt flat as market winds down before break.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ debt markets wind down to dull close ahead of break
* Money market weakens on thin flows
* Next focus inflation data due on January 17
New Zealand bond yields were slightly higher in late afternoon trade on Tuesday as the market wound down for a two-day break for the New Year holiday.

The money market weakened slightly in thin trade on the back of end of year book-squaring. The 90-day bank bills edging up three basis points to 7.90 percent and the March futures contract slipping six to 92.56.
"There is probably more life on Mars than there is in this market," one dealer said.

Little action is expected until market attention begins to focus on key inflation data due out on January 17. Volumes are seen picking up next week as traders return from holiday, but some suggest it could be the third week of January before activity climbs back to normal levels.
